reasons: Limits are checked in the browser in the visible code, and server checks were not visible.
Sub-role name lists are hard-coded and need manual updates.
The value labelled average points is the average of a batting or bowling stat called avg, which may mislead.
Only ten of the thirteen sections were visible in this review, so the rest of the list rendering is unexplained.

terms.meaning: a squad a player picks from real players, which scores points based on how those players perform
the budget value each player costs, with a fixed total the team must stay under
the coin flip at the start of a match that decides which side bats first
a finer grouping inside a role, such as spinner or opener
a group of eleven players, a full cricket side

sections.name: File setup, Stat, Player
sections.title: Imports and player shape
sections.what: Brings in React tools, the router, icons, and the limits from the rules file. Defines the shape of a player, including stats and an optional sub-role.
sections.why: Likely reason: the rules come from one shared file so the screen and server can agree.
sections.watch_out: Limits come from another file, so changing the rules file changes this screen.

sections.name: getSubRole, RoleFilter
sections.title: Sub-role labels
sections.what: Sorts batsmen into opener or middle order, and bowlers into spin, fast pace or medium pace, by checking each player's name against fixed lists. Also defines the role filter names.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the visitor filter by a finer role. Otherwise not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Matching by name text means a new or renamed player is labelled wrongly until the lists are updated.

sections.name: ROLE_REQUIREMENTS
sections.title: Role limits and labels
sections.what: Combines each role's minimum and maximum from the rules file with a short label for the screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps role labels in one place on this screen.
sections.watch_out: Depends on min and max values existing in the rules file.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 1)
sections.title: Component start and selection totals
sections.what: Accepts the players and match details. Sets up memory for the chosen players, captain, vice-captain, current step, submit state, error and role filter. Totals the credits and counts each role.
sections.why: Likely reason: the screen must track the selection to enforce the rules.
sections.watch_out: Totals are recalculated on every change, so the numbers follow the selection list.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient: if
sections.title: Adding, removing and checking the team
sections.what: Toggling a player: removing one also clears captain or vice-captain if needed. Adding is refused when eleven players, the credit budget or a role maximum would be broken. Continue requires exactly eleven players and the minimum of each role. Submit requires a captain and a different vice-captain, then starts the request to /api/team.
sections.why: Likely reason: invalid teams are stopped early.
sections.watch_out: These are the only visible rules, so the server must repeat them.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 3)
sections.title: Submit result and player sorting
sections.what: After the request, a success sends the visitor to the crew page and refreshes. A failure shows the server's message, and a network failure shows a network message. Players are filtered by role and sorted with the playing eleven first once the toss is done, then by credits.
sections.why: Likely reason: the most useful players are shown first.
sections.watch_out: The playing eleven is only given priority after the toss, so before the toss there is no priority.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 4)
sections.title: Sidebar: credits, count and role progress
sections.what: Shows credits left in a bar that turns red under fifteen credits, the player count, and one bar per role showing progress toward its minimum and maximum. The continue button is enabled only when the team is valid.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the visitor a live view of what remains.
sections.watch_out: The red warning uses a fixed fifteen-credit threshold, not a value from the rules file.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 5)
sections.title: Captain step and confirm
sections.what: Explains that the captain earns double points and the vice-captain one and a half times. Shows the chosen names, a confirm button, and a back button to the roster.
sections.why: Likely reason: choosing the captain is a separate decision from picking players.
sections.watch_out: The multipliers are fixed text here, so a rule change must be made here and on the server.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 6)
sections.title: Error message and chosen list
sections.what: Shows the latest error in a pulsing red box. In the selection step, lists the chosen players with role, credits and a remove button.
sections.why: Likely reason: errors are visible and the visitor can fix the selection.
sections.watch_out: The error stays until the next valid action clears it, so an old message can linger.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 7)
sections.title: Roster header, toss status and role filter
sections.what: Shows the ROSTER heading and whether the toss is done. Shows role tabs with the count of chosen and total players for each role. Starts the player list, computing each row's sub-role and an average value. The rows are only partly visible in this review.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the visitor narrow the list by role and see how many they have picked.
sections.watch_out: The value labelled average points is actually the average of the stat called avg, not fantasy points, so the label can mislead.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 8)
sections.title: Player rows with selection state
sections.what: Draws each player in the picking list as a clickable row showing role icon, name, team, sub-role label, credits and average points. Chosen players get a red border and a tick icon. After the toss, playing players get a green dot and benched players are dimmed with a red dot.
sections.why: Likely reason: the user needs to see at a glance who is picked and who is still playing after the toss.
sections.watch_out: The sub-role colours come from a chain of conditions, so a new sub-role label that is not in that list shows as plain grey.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 9)
sections.title: Captain and vice-captain picker
sections.what: Lists the selected squad with two buttons per player, C for captain and VC for vice-captain. A note on the panel says captain points count double and vice-captain points count 1.5 times. A player can hold only one of the two roles.
sections.why: Likely reason: the captain choice is made after the squad is picked, and the note explains what the choice is worth.
sections.watch_out: The 2x and 1.5x multipliers are typed into the labels here, so if the scoring rule changes these labels must change too.

sections.name: TeamBuilderClient (part 10)
sections.title: Vice-captain button and closing
sections.what: Holds the VC button for each player. Choosing VC for a player who is captain clears captain, and the captain button does the reverse. It also closes the lists and the component.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the two roles separate so one player cannot count twice.
sections.watch_out: The two buttons clear each other's role, so removing either side of that logic would let one player hold both roles.

summary: The team builder where a visitor picks eleven players within a credit budget and role limits, names a captain and vice-captain, and submits the team.
purpose: Lets a player build their fantasy eleven for a match and submit it.
why: Likely reason: a two-step flow catches mistakes before submission.
how: 1. The visitor picks players, tracked with a running credit total and role counts. 2. Rules stop adding too many players, too many credits, or too many of one role. 3. Continue needs exactly eleven players and the minimum of each role. 4. On the captain step, the visitor chooses a captain and a different vice-captain, then confirms, which sends the team to /api/team. 5. On success, the visitor goes to the crew page. On failure, the message is shown. The list is sorted with the playing eleven first once the toss is done, then by credits.
inputs: The player list with roles, credits and stats, the match id, crew id, toss status, and team names.
outputs: A POST request to /api/team, navigation to the crew page on success, and error messages.
risks: The limits are enforced in the browser in the visible code. The server must check them again, which is not visible here. Sub-role name lists are fixed in the code.
debug: If Continue stays disabled, compare the role counts with the minimums. If a submit fails, read the message in the reply and check /api/team. If credits look wrong, check each player's credits and the MAX_CREDITS value.
